elements.text: • All excursions, entrance fees & guided tours included
• Audio headsets included on Days 2 to 4
• St Bavo Cathedral & ‘The Adoration of the Mystic Lamb’
• Ghent Museum of Fine Arts – guided tour
• Palais des Beaux Arts at Lille – guided tour

We stay four nights at the centrally located 4* Dukes’ Academie Hotel (https://www.dukesacademie.com/) in Bruges. Located under a fifteen minute walk from the market square, facilities at the hotel include a breakfast room and bar. All rooms are en suite and feature television, tea & coffee making facilities, and an in room safe. A set three course dinner without drinks is included at the Maximiliaan van Oostenrijk Restaurant (located a 100 metres walk from the hotel) on the first evening. The remaining three nights are on a bed and breakfast basis.
Price based on twin share. Minimum numbers required. Normal booking conditions apply.
For more information on this tour contact your Group Organiser

We depart by executive coach from our designated pick up point and
travel with our tour manager to Folkestone for our Eurotunnel crossing to
Calais. On arrival in Bruges we check into the 4* Dukes’ Academie Hotel for a four night stay. A welcome dinner is included at a restaurant close to
This morning, we enjoy an included guided walking tour of Bruges, whose
historic city centre is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Known as the
‘Venice of the North’, Bruges is famous for lace making, chocolate and its picturesque network of canals. An included 45 minute cruise on the
picturesque canals of Bruges enables us to see the city from a different perspective. This afternoon we visit the Groeninge Museum in Bruges,
home to a fine collection of Flemish and Belgian painting from Jan Van
Eyck to Marcel Broodthears, a wide range of Renaissance and Baroque
Masters and representations of Belgian Symbolism and Modernism.
Our morning guided tour of Antwerp takes in sights such as the Great Market Square, Town Hall, Butchers’ Guild House and the Cathedral of
Ghent Museum of Fine Arts Our Lady. This afternoon we visit Rubens House, the former house of
Peter Rubens from 1616 until his death in 1640. The house was built
Palais des Beaux Arts at Lille around an inner courtyard and the Baroque portico between the

courtyard and the Flemish-Italian Renaissance garden was designed by the master himself. Our guided tour of the House introduces us to the life and works of Rubens, including his self portrait, ‘Adam and Eve in Paradise’, ‘Henry IV in the battle for Paris’ and a portrait of Sir Anthony Van Dyck as a boy.
We visit Ghent this morning for a guided walking tour. Originally the
capital of Flanders, Ghent retains more historical buildings than any other

Flemish city. Here we visit St Bavo Cathedral, which is home to the famous 24-panel altarpiece ‘The Adoration of the Mystic Lamb’. This afternoon we have a guided tour at the Ghent Museum of Fine Arts with works ranging from 19th century Realism, Romanticism, Impressionism, Symbolism and Expressionism to 20th century Surrealism, including two works by Hieronymus Bosch.
After checking out of our hotel we enjoy a guided tour at the Palais des

Beaux Arts at Lille, considered by many to be one of France’s most important galleries. Taking carefully selected comfort stops en route, we return to Calais for our return Eurotunnel crossing to Folkestone, and onwards coach travel back to our original pick up point.
NB:- Due to regulations in Bruges, coaches have restricted access within the city centre.

On the first and last days of the tour, the coach will drop us off at a designated point which is less than a three minute walk away from the hotel. Porterage between the coach and hotel is included in the cost of the tour (one piece of luggage per person). Please note we reserve the right to alter the above itinerary if required for operational reasons. Given the historic nature of the places visited, a certain degree of walking will be involved, and this holiday may not be suitable for those with mobility problems.
